title: Centralize misroute guard into shared function to prevent drift
context: Issue #54 identified a bug where agents forget cwd, silently committing work to the wrong checkout when files exist in linked worktrees. PR #63 added protection to hunch_record_decision, but hunch_record_correction and hunch_record_finding have identical shape, root cause, and blast radius yet remained unprotected. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extract the misroute refusal logic into a single misrouteGuard() function called by all three auto-committing write tools (src/mcp/server.ts). How each tool's file evidence gets to that shared check evolved across review: an initial attempt exported repoRelativeHint so hunch_record_correction could relativize an absolute scope_hint_file against root before checking -- superseded by dec_d09ab8e9a0, which found that approach didn't actually work for the realistic case (an agent's own worktree-rooted absolute path) and replaced it with existsUnder/deepestContainer, understanding absolute paths directly rather than relativizing them. repoRelativeHint is private again; see dec_d09ab8e9a0 for the current design.
consequences: One source of truth for misroute detection and refusal messaging; future changes propagate uniformly
All three tools now enforce the same guard and use identical language, eliminating inconsistency
Added tests verify the guard works for hunch_record_correction, hunch_record_finding, and hunch_record_decision, including absolute-path and no-false-positive cases
alternatives_rejected: Duplicate the guard logic in each tool (risks drift as behavior evolves)
Apply the guard inconsistently to only hunch_record_decision (leaves identical tools unprotected)
